definition: The standard classical Arabic and Islamic jurisprudential term for sexual intercourse, derived from the root j-m-ʿ ('to come together/assemble'); used in fiqh, hadith commentary, and traditional medical writing.
notes: Preferred term in Islamic legal texts (fiqh); not used in everyday conversation due to cultural taboo but recognized by educated MSA speakers across the Arab world.

definition: Modern MSA compound for sexual intercourse, literally 'sexual contact/connection'; used in public health, sex education, and journalism across the Arab world.
notes: Calque-style modern coinage; more neutral and impersonal than مجامعة; common in media, health campaigns, and academic writing.

definition: The primary and most common vulgar Arabic verb for sexual intercourse, equivalent in force and ubiquity to English 'fuck'; used as both verb and noun.
notes: The single most iconic Arabic sexual expletive; universally recognized across all Arabic-speaking regions and dialects regardless of education level; extremely taboo in formal or mixed-gender contexts.

definition: Nomen vicis (instance noun) of نيك; denotes a single act or instance of sexual intercourse, formed by the standard Arabic instance-noun suffix -a.
notes: As crude as the base verb نيك; the morphological instance-noun form is a standard Arabic pattern making this derivation entirely transparent to native speakers.

definition: Literally 'to trample or tread heavily upon'; used as crude slang for sexual intercourse with emphasis on forceful, dominating penetration.
notes: Base meaning is physical trampling; sexual use evokes aggression and physical dominance over the passive partner; more common in Egyptian and Levantine colloquial speech than formal MSA.

definition: Literally 'to cork, stopper, or plug a bottle'; used crudely for sexual penetration, emphasizing the act of filling or blocking an orifice.
notes: Bottle-and-cork metaphor; recognition is lower and more dialect-specific than نيك; more common in Gulf and Levantine colloquial registers; the sexual meaning requires context.

definition: Literally 'to enter'; the most widespread classical and colloquial Arabic euphemism for sexual penetration or marital consummation; used in religious texts, law, and everyday speech.
notes: Has formal legal significance in Islamic fiqh regarding marriage consummation (الدخول بالزوجة); the euphemistic sexual sense is understood universally by Arabic speakers of all registers.

definition: Literally 'to stab, pierce, or thrust'; used crudely for vigorous or aggressive sexual intercourse, evoking the forceful thrusting action of penetration.
notes: Violent stabbing metaphor applied to sex; evokes aggressive male-dominant penetration; more colloquial than standard MSA but the sexual meaning is widely understood in context.

definition: Literally 'to ride or mount'; used crudely for sexual intercourse with emphasis on the active, mounting partner; applies primarily to the dominant-on-top position.
notes: Equestrian metaphor; the sexual meaning of ركب is broadly understood across Arabic dialects; attested in classical Arabic erotica including Thousand and One Nights; can imply either partner depending on framing.

definition: The generic Arabic verb 'to do'; used as a minimal contextual euphemism for sexual intercourse by referring to the act without naming it.
notes: Functions like English 'to do it'; attested in hadith literature as a discreet reference to the sex act; the sexual meaning is entirely context-dependent as the word has no inherent sexual sense.

definition: Literally 'to touch'; a classical Quranic and hadith euphemism for sexual intercourse, denoting physical union through the gentlest possible abstraction.
notes: Used in the Quran (e.g. Q2:237, Q33:49) in phrases meaning 'before you have touched them' to denote consummation of marriage; the most elevated and religiously sanctioned Arabic euphemism for sex; essentially obsolete outside Quranic quotation.

definition: Literally 'to hit, beat, or strike'; used crudely for sexual intercourse with emphasis on forceful, aggressive thrusting or physical domination.
notes: One of several impact-verb metaphors applied to sex in Arabic; less iconic than نيك but broadly understood in sexual context; more common in Egyptian and Levantine colloquial than formal MSA.

definition: Literally 'to dig or excavate'; used crudely for sexual intercourse, evoking deep, repetitive penetrating action.
notes: Digging/excavation metaphor emphasizes depth and repetition of penetration; lower recognition than more common crude intercourse terms; more colloquial than formal MSA registers.

definition: Literally 'sucking the penis'; a descriptive clinical compound using القضيب, the classical and medical Arabic term for penis, to denote fellatio.
notes: القضيب is the standard classical/medical word for penis (also means 'rod/staff' in non-sexual usage); the phrase is sexually explicit but uses anatomical rather than vulgar lexeme for penis, keeping it in a clinical register.

definition: Literally 'oral sex'; the modern MSA clinical compound for any form of oral sexual contact, covering both fellatio and cunnilingus.
notes: Modern calque of English 'oral sex'; used in public health literature, sex education materials, and journalism; the most neutral and clinical MSA term for the oral-sex category; gender-neutral.

definition: Literally 'oral foreplay' or 'oral caressing/stimulation'; an MSA clinical-euphemistic compound used in health and educational contexts for oral sexual activity.
notes: مداعبة ('caressing, fondling, foreplay') softens the explicitness; used interchangeably with الجنس الفموي in clinical writing but carries a slightly more euphemistic and less direct flavor; gender-neutral.

definition: Literally 'kissing/sucking the dick'; crude colloquial compound for fellatio using زب, one of the most common vulgar Arabic words for penis.
notes: زب is among the most widely recognized vulgar terms for penis in Egyptian and Levantine Arabic; بوس in colloquial usage means both 'to kiss' and 'to suck'; extremely offensive in formal or mixed contexts.

definition: Onomatopoeic word derived from the repeated sucking or slurping sound (root م-ص repeated); used crudely for fellatio, emphasizing the oral suction action.
notes: The reduplication pattern م-ص-م-ص mimics the sound of sucking; the word exists in non-sexual contexts (sucking on candy) but in a sexual context unambiguously denotes fellatio; the onomatopoeia intensifies the crudeness.

definition: Literally 'licking the dick'; crude compound for oral penis stimulation using الزب, a highly vulgar colloquial term for penis.
notes: لعق emphasizes licking rather than full oral insertion or suction, making it slightly more specific than مص; زب marks the register as highly crude; widely understood across Egyptian and Levantine Arabic-speaking populations.

definition: Literally 'sucking the cock'; highly crude compound for fellatio using الأير (al-ayr), one of the most offensive and taboo Arabic terms for penis.
notes: أير (ayr) is among the most taboo and offensive Arabic words for penis, comparable to English 'cock' in crude force and carrying stronger transgressive weight than زب in most dialects; this compound sits at the extreme crude end of fellatio vocabulary.

definition: Literally 'licking of the vulva/vagina'; a semi-clinical MSA phrase for cunnilingus using الفرج, the classical and anatomical Arabic term for the external female genitalia.
notes: الفرج is the standard classical/clinical Arabic term for the external female genitalia; the phrase is sexually explicit but uses anatomical rather than street-slang vocabulary; found in classical erotic literature (e.g. The Perfumed Garden) and modern clinical texts.

definition: Literally 'sucking the vulva/vagina'; a clinical-register phrase for cunnilingus using الفرج, the standard classical Arabic anatomical term for the female genital area.
notes: Parallel construction to مص القضيب (fellatio); both pair مص ('to suck') with the clinical anatomical term for the relevant genitalia; explicit but does not use street-level slang for the anatomy.

definition: Literally 'female oral sex'; a clinical MSA phrase for cunnilingus, distinguishing it from the gender-neutral الجنس الفموي by the addition of الأنثوي ('female/feminine').
notes: The most clinical and academic MSA designation for cunnilingus; the three-word construction makes it unwieldy in ordinary speech; most likely to appear in sexology, public health, or academic texts; recognition lower than simpler constructions.

definition: Literally 'oral stimulation/foreplay for the woman'; a clinical-euphemistic MSA phrase for cunnilingus, the feminine-specific parallel to the gender-neutral مداعبة فموية.
notes: The periphrastic structure and use of مداعبة ('caressing/foreplay') make this suitable for health education materials; the phrase avoids naming any anatomical part, maximizing politeness at the cost of specificity; lower street recognition than any crude term.

definition: Literally 'licking'; used crudely as shorthand for cunnilingus; the bare verb evoking oral stimulation of the female genitalia without specifying the anatomy.
notes: لحس in non-sexual contexts means simply 'to lick' (food, wounds, etc.); in sexual context it defaults to cunnilingus; its brevity and anatomy-free construction make it slightly less transgressive than compounds explicitly naming the vulva, but it is widely understood as crude.
